title: Learning to Assemble Novel Structures with Unfamiliar Parts under Semantic Constraints
abstract: arXiv:2608.13684v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper describes a neurosymbolic architecture for learning to assemble novel structures using evidence from embodied conversations and task demonstrations. We focus on scenarios where an agent encounters, after deployment, semantic constraints on structures--in other words, constraints as to which part types and features make valid structures--that were not available during training, and where it is initially unaware of the relevant structure and component part concepts. The agent must acquire and exploit such knowledge through user interactions while attempting assembly. We study this setting in a simulated toy truck assembly domain, learning from symbolic evidence encoded in natural language and from dense visual observations. Our experiments show that communicating semantic constraints through natural language (e.g., "dump trucks have a dumper") yields more data-efficient online adaptation than relying only on task demonstrations

translated_title: 在不熟悉零件与语义约束下学习组装新型结构
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13684v1 公告类型：新 摘要：本文描述了一种神经符号架构，用于通过具身对话和任务演示中的证据学习组装新型结构。我们聚焦于这样的场景：智能体在部署后遇到结构上的语义约束——即关于哪些零件类型和特征构成有效结构的约束——这些约束在训练时不可用，且智能体最初对相关结构和组件零件概念一无所知。智能体必须在尝试组装过程中通过用户交互获取并利用此类知识。我们在一个模拟玩具卡车组装领域研究了这一设置，从自然语言编码的符号证据和密集视觉观察中学习。我们的实验表明，通过自然语言传达语义约束（例如，“自卸卡车有一个翻斗”）比仅依赖任务演示能实现更高效的数据在线适应。
tldr: 本文提出一种神经符号架构，使智能体在部署后通过自然语言语义约束而非仅依赖演示，更高效地学习组装带有未知零件和新型结构。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a neurosymbolic architecture enabling agents to learn assembling novel structures with unfamiliar parts more efficiently via natural language semantic constraints after deployment, rather than relying solely on demonstrations.
